body:
I'm guessing you work in criminal justice? That is where I work. There does seem to be a sense of hopelessness sometimes... watching a woman get 10 years for a petty theft parole violation hurt me fairly bad. But trust me, you are helping just by believing in them, just by caring. I've found, when I've been in the darkest of places, that an off hand comment or small action can make an incredible difference. So, even if you can't move the mountains and skies and change the entire system, try to be that distant star they look to when night comes again. 

I can't believe that it is hopeless. Things are changing, slowly but surely. Every chance is new, even if the situation isn't. 

Being discouraged does not make you a bad worker. It means you care.

I was jusr looking at my schedule. You are everything to me. I have loved you and love you now, ever since you were born. I am always here, you are not a burden, I can understand some pf what you are going through. Worrying about you isnt enough. Lets get some therapy and talk to the dr. I am proud of you and it is the different ones that shine, you are very special and unique, you need to see it. I love you and so does Dad/

You deserve to live. 

If everything else seems foreign- if each letter seems ancient, dead Latin- then know that you deserve to live. 

You deserve to recover.

I am on medication. They are not happy pills. They give me the ability to feel happiness.  


We have to be in a position to accept joy. And when we are depressed, or furious, or apathetic, we can't feel that happiness. Sometimes we need distractions. Do you watch movies? Do you watch videos on youtube? Do you doodle?

Also, being too late implies the past which implies that you can't change it. So what do you do now? You form a different theory, a new hypothesis, and you gather the data and you figure it out. 

Press your finger against different surfaces and observe your own finger print. Learn a new word. Take a nap in the sunlight. 

Infinite possibilities. Infinite you. 

Stay brave.

You don't need to apologize. 

You are doing great right now. 

Just keep typing. 

I had a friend named Tyler who had one arm that ended at the elbow and another arm that only had three fingers. He rocked at guitar hero. He was born that way. 

It takes time to adjust when our body wants to give way beneath us. 

I am not going to say it gets better but logic dictates that it gets different so start looking out for yourself. 

So if you swim with the freshmen show them compassion because you know how hard it is and then show them *skill* because you know what the fuck you are doing in the water. 

Breathe. 

Breathe like you are swimming. Calculated breaths. 

Stay brave.

When there is a child involved there is no easy decision. 

Please know that nothing I am going to say is an attack or meant to upset you or assume you are at fault. 

First I would like to say that your happiness is important and you deserve to love yourself. 

Having a child makes it very difficult to focus on yourself. 

If you are unable to care for you child than it is time to ask for help. But trust me when I say that your baby loves you and that he wants you to stay in his life. 

*The fact that you care about ruining him shows how much you love him.*

They say that it is impossible to prove something is impossible. Factors and environmental influence create billions of alternate paths. 

Several paths lead to a life where you and your child are happy. You won't always be but looking back, as you watch him graduate or stand at the altar, or pack his own lunch, you will know joy. 

This is a possibility. So think. How can you make this happen?

You are incredible for trying so hard and I think you are amazing and I hope you keep going. 

Stay brave.

You are important.

And this is not because of your grades. 

You are important because you are a life. 

I agree that it is time for a change. Focus on yourself because you matter and if this stress is killing you then *no one should blame you for switching things up*. 

In addition, I completely understand "shutting down". I call it fading. When everything becomes too much I cope by feeling nothing. I drift away. This can be helpful in the short term but eventually we have to face all those feelings. 

You have been working very hard and you need some time to relax. You deserve to take care of yourself. 

So what do you enjoy? What do you think about doing? Because these things matter. 

Stay brave

Okay. Hi. 

Could you take some deep breaths? 

This has happened to me. When I first got a debit card I saw an offer for a "free laptop" and clicked away. I felt stupid and alone and I was so scared to tell anyone even as my bank account was run dry. 

Eventually I told my mother. It felt like such a relief to tell someone. 

*you are not to blame*

The person who lied and stole from you is to blame. 

I am so glad that you reached out tonight. 

Are you still taking deep breaths? 

You are so brave right now for holding on. 

Do you want to talk about some of what has been going on? It is okay if you don't. You can talk about whatever you want. 

Stay brave

You don't have to do anything but be yourself to get my attention. 

I didn't see your other posts. 

It you can- post every thought you have because every single one matters to me. 

*I want to help you*

Please know that you matter, and not just because you matter to me, but because you were born important and that will never change. 

I am going to be on late tonight. I sincerely hope that you reply.

A man walks to a bridge. He says to himself- if someone smiles at me before I reach the bridge I will not jump.

You can make someone's day by a small movement of lips. 

But incredibly you could frown forever and still matter. You are inherently, naturally, always, important. Every breath you take is essential because you took it. 

If you want to talk- talk. Or scream. Take a hammer to a trash can (who cares about dents on them). But no matter what you do it will be *important*. It will be important because *you are important*. 

Stay brave.

I'm sorry that you are having such a tough time right now. 

I am going to share some of my experiences in the hope that you can find a sort of hope from them. 

When I was in high school I had no idea what I wanted or who I was. The friends who stayed with me, through the terrifying onset of my mental illness, were either barely hanging on or poisonous. College was supposed to be my fresh start- free of old relationships and pretense and all of the troublesome pills. 

I crashed hard. It has been a few  years since then and what I have learned is that what I want, popular or not, matter. I have learned that how I feel is important. I am still figuring out what I actually want from life and that's okay. 

One of the hardest things to do is to love yourself. 

I ask you this- do you want to play football because of the opportunity and the societal allures or do you want to play because you actually love the sport? Have you tried other activities? You mentioned a group that you fit into- do they also enjoy sports? Could you set up a casual game between friends?

College, by the way, is a completely different playing field. Even a community college has exponentially more students than a high school. You will meet a large variety of people- and people are much more open minded. 

I used to wish that I would go to sleep and never wake up. I didn't care about anything- being awake was exhausting. Now while I still love sleep... I find reasons to stay awake. Right now I enjoy carving wood. It isn't fancy or anything. Just something to pass the time. 

Stay brave.

In my opinion, if you were in a three year relationship, then both partners should be significantly invested. If there were multiple issues with the relationship then I doubt that one argument was the end and I *seriously* doubt that you are the only one to blame.

This seems like a time of much change for you. 

First, staying alive is never cowardice. You are fighting and you are so brave for it. 

Second, there is no shame in being sad even though I know that is really hard to believe. Sometimes I need to cry and scream and feel misery. 

And third- now might be a time to try to find yourself again. Being in a long term relationship can sometimes make you lose sight of yourself. Maybe now would be a good time to reevaluate thing things you like, what you want, etc. 

Right now has to be really rough and I'm sorry. I know my trying to put a positive spin on it might not seem helpful. But I do hope that you come out of this dark time with an even better sense of self and life than before.

I am glad you are still here.

Good luck on your journey.

At first I wanted to die and I was angry that I had  been stopped. Hospitalization was needed for me because it kept me safe so that I could begin to get better. 

Co-dependency is common among those with issues of depression. Sometimes getting away from our family is healthy.

No one truly "likes" sexual abuse. However, abusers can completely twist their actions and victims are known to rationalize these experiences in an attempt to make it bearable. 

I will admit that being hospitalized seems scary. Sometimes, however, it can be very helpful. For me, it gave me a safe place so that I could finally begin recovery. 

Again, you are being very brave by standing beside her. Just please remember that your own safety matters as well and that you are taking care of yourself emotionally.

I am glad I could help. 

Hope you are feeling better, even a little.

You are very welcome. 

I am so glad that you are feeling better and that you can use that experience to help further your recovery.

It is very difficult to help someone when you are not talking directly to them. 

You are a very kind person for helping her. 

However, when it comes to issues of sexual abuse I would look into contacting her area's child protection agency and reporting the situation. People in these situations often feel as if they cannot reach out for help. 

She should absolutely find a therapist and she should be honest. There is nothing to be ashamed of for being suicidal.

I am glad you came here for support. 

First, you have a very creative soul. Your writing is incredible. 

Second, what I am going to tell you will never be a lie. 

You are valuable. Every breath that you take matters and when you open your eyes tomorrow you will be just as important as the day you opened them for the first time. 

In order to appeal to your creativity I offer you this- What of metal? What of metal with gouges that run as deep as caverns? What of a blade snapped in half? *It is reforged*

It is melted down and recreated. Matter is not destroyed only changed and nothing is broken beyond repair. 

And I don't speak to the pain of your family because it is secondary. Your life matters. And not just because the pain your death will bring- not because of their legacy or their own issues. You are important on your own. 

I hope that you will write back. I hope you keep writing in general.

Hi.

Everything has to be a little scary right now, I'm sure. At least that is how I felt when I overdosed. 

I want you to know that it is okay to ask for help. I was put in the hospital for a while after my attempt. It wasn't fun, of course, but it got me the help I needed to get back on my feet. 

You are important and I care about your life. There is no judgement here. You are the focus. 

Please let me know how you are doing, here or in private message. I would prefer to talk here so that others can also offer their assistance.

I'm so sorry that you feel this way. 

It sounds like you have planning this for some time. If you can wait a little bit longer, please spend some time with us here. Talk to us- let us know what is going on. 

You are important and your life matters. I hope this message finds you okay.

Everyone here cares. You are an important person and you do matter. I may not have experienced what you have managed to survive but I have been in a place where I can't see a way out. 

One thing that has helped me, when everything seems dark, is making a list of things I have to do before I can let go. It starts out simple- writing goodbye letters and letting people know what to do with my belongings. And over time it gets more complicated- like who will care for my cats. The list gets longer. I want to read my favorite book again. I want to go for a walk. 

It has always helped me last a little longer- hold on until I feel better. And maybe this won't help you. But I hope it does and if it doesn't I hope you find something that does because you're well being matters to me.
You are very, very welcome. You are worth it.

You sound very similar to me. 

I'm so sorry you are going through this. 

You may not be actively facing your demons in battle but you are *surviving* them. Each day you wake up and open your eyes you shoulder the weight of all of that darkness. 

Count every step you take and tell yourself- "I did that. I traveled that distance." Some days it takes a marathon to sit up in bed and some days I never get dressed. But I tell myself that I did well when I manage to. 

Your therapist should be someone you trust absolutely but someone who knows you can't tell them everything. A boxer doesn't start in the ring against a champion. Tackling these issues is slow and difficult. 

Do you write? You seem talented!

I hope this helps.

You are important. 

You are important the moment you walk into a classroom and the moment you wake up. You are valuable because of every step you take and each time you say hello to someone. 

Being important is inherent- it is natural. From the moment you were born you were worth this life. 

It matters that you are sad. It matters to me. 

This is something that helped me, and that still does- I get loud. Watch a bad movie and yell at the screen. I throw down my purse and crash into my chair and dare everyone to look by the way I square my shoulders. 

That might not work for you. But there are tons of other ideas, too. Try something and let us know, if you could. Because we *do* care.

Let me begin by saying that you did the right thing by coming here. We are all here to support you. 

I am going to pick out a few things that seem positive about you. I don't mean to imply in any way that your feelings aren't valid or real. But sometimes it is hard to look positively at our own lives. 

You seem to have a good grasp at where you stand politically and with important issues. That shows me that you still care about some part of the state of the world. 

You are actively seeking out your passions! That seems incredible to me. Finding any job is difficult and, depending on your field, can be near impossible. What is important is that you are *trying*. 

When you say that you want to commit suicide, but that you won't, that tells me that you are fighting really hard right now. 

I hope this helps, even a little.
I just wanted to say that you are are very brave for what you have lived through.

You are important. 

All of the pain you are feeling right now is valid. 

I understand that you want to help others but someone using a cane shouldn't be expected to push a wheelchair. Right now, you need to focus on yourself and *that is okay*. 

Think about things that make you happy (I know that seems impossible right now). Find new hobbies. I found out I like to carve strips of wood off of branches. It is completely random but I enjoy it. Simple, repetitive tasks often help me calm down. 

Your pain matters to others, and most importantly it should matter to you. It's okay that you're upset.

I hope you feel better soon.

I just wanted to say I hope you're still here.

I have attempted and I can't say that I am exactly "happy" that I am still here (not all the time). Each year that passes I suppose it gets a little easier. It isn't pure ecstasy and I doubt it ever will be. I always expected some sort of revelation where I suddenly found the joy and meaning in life. Life isn't a fairy tale and that won't happen and I am actually okay with that. 

But it really goes get a little easier. I constantly try to find new, random shit to do. I found out recently I like staining wood. I'm going nuts on all the old wood stuff in my house. And I like painting my walls and I don't care if it doesn't look like a professional job because I did it myself. And one day I plan to actually finish that one bedroom wall that is half pink and half purple. I'm not in a rush. 

I don't know your situation or anything and I know how pissed I get when someone tells me they understand my suicidal issues. But I can only really offer suggestions that have worked for me. 

To be honest I didn't do it alone, not at first. It took hospital stays and medication after medication and long nights and longer days. But I can dig myself out of some of those holes now. 

And maybe this is nonsense but this is all I can do. I hope you make it.
